dersimelagon.text: Tanning-focused circles follow dersimelagon because it is an oral MC1R agonist that darkens skin pigment, in the way of melanocortin tanning peptides. It was developed for light-sensitivity disorders, so any use for a cosmetic tan is off-label, and no trials have looked at appearance.

semax.text: Semax is used in study-maxxing and nootropic circles for focus, learning and neuroprotection, not for appearance. Forum posters sometimes mention libido as a side benefit. Human evidence consists of small stroke trials in Russia, and no appearance effect has been studied.

chain: Fewer fine lines, more even tone
hydroxypinacolone-retinoate.text: HPR, sold as Granactive Retinoid, is used as a gentler cosmetic retinoid for fine lines and dark spots, often by people who find retinol irritating. Published human data are small and mostly come from combination products rather than HPR alone.

chain: Converts to retinoic acid in skin
retinaldehyde-retinal.text: Retinal is used in over-the-counter serums as a middle step between retinol and prescription tretinoin, for wrinkles and uneven tone. Skin-specific human evidence is sparse, with most studies being older or still registered.

chain: Clearer skin on face and trunk
trifarotene-aklief.text: Aklief is a prescription retinoid cream used for acne on the face, chest and back, and users discuss it as a step before isotretinoin. Its acne use is studied in large vehicle-controlled trials and is FDA-approved; no anti-aging approval exists.

chain: Converted to retinol, then retinoic acid
retinyl-palmitate.text: Retinyl palmitate is the vitamin A ester found in moisturisers and sunscreens, and some users treat it as the gentlest retinoid for skin aging. It is the least-studied cosmetic retinoid for wrinkles, and its use on sun-exposed skin has been debated for years.

chain: Fuller cheeks, softer folds, defined contours
poly-l-lactic-acid-sculptra.text: Sculptra is injected to restore cheek and midface volume, soften cheek lines, and rebuild a gaunt face after weight loss, with results building gradually over weeks. Randomized trials and systematic reviews report effects lasting up to about two years.

deoxycholic-acid-kybella.text: Kybella is an injectable approved for reducing a double chin, used to sharpen the jaw and neck line without surgery. Fat removal in the treated area is visible once swelling settles, and some users also ask about other small fat pads.

chain: Lasting volume in chin, cheeks, scars
polymethyl-methacrylate-pmma-filler.text: PMMA filler (Artefill, Bellafill) is injected for permanent volume in the cheeks and chin and to lift acne scars, so the result is visible straight away and stays. Outcome data are limited, and bodybuilders have also injected PMMA-type products for muscle size.

poly-d-l-lactic-acid-pdlla.text: PDLLA is a collagen-stimulating injectable used for skin quality, wrinkles and acne scar texture, related to PLLA. Improvements build up gradually over weeks. A handful of trials exist, and nodules are the main known risk.

collagen-filler.text: Collagen filler is the original injectable, used to soften wrinkles and fold lines and to add lip volume, with the plumping visible right after treatment. It is temporary, bovine versions can provoke allergies, and hyaluronic acid has largely replaced it.

polyacrylamide-gel.text: Polyacrylamide gel is a permanent injectable that has been used for facial contouring and for HIV-related facial fat loss, with volume visible once placed. Published cosmetic evidence is thin in the sources reviewed, and removal can be difficult.

mercury-skin-lightening.text: Mercury-containing creams and soaps are used in informal markets to pale skin and fade dark spots. Mercury salts do inhibit melanin production. They are banned in many countries and have no clinical cosmetic use.

clobetasol-propionate.text: Clobetasol is a prescription steroid for conditions such as psoriasis and eczema. It appears as a hidden ingredient in illicit lightening creams, where lightening is a side effect of its action on skin. Its use for lightening is off-label and unstudied.

decapeptide-12.text: Decapeptide-12 is a cosmetic peptide marketed for brightening and fading hyperpigmentation, with users comparing it to hydroquinone. Evidence consists of small, uncontrolled studies, often on multi-ingredient products, and skin penetration is a known limit.

chain: Starch and amino acids on skin
rice-water.text: Rice water is a folk beauty rinse from parts of Asia, used on hair and as a skin wash for glow and an even tone. It is popular in beauty communities, and no trials have tested it for hair or skin.

chain: Believed to calm and fade blemishes
turmeric-topical.text: Turmeric pastes and masks are a long-standing South Asian preparation, promoted in appearance communities for brightening and evening skin tone and fading blemishes. One small vitiligo trial exists, none address cosmetic lightening, and the pigment can stain skin.

powdered-pearl.text: Powdered pearl has about two thousand years of use in Chinese medicine for a luminous complexion, applied as a mask or taken by mouth. Research covers wound and bone repair, and its use for skin brightening is based on tradition.

trenbolone.text: Trenbolone is a veterinary steroid used by bodybuilders for muscle mass, strength and a lean, hard look. Forum posters also claim effects on height and facial structure. There are no human trials, and reviews of users report adverse effects in most.

chain: Greater lean mass and joint comfort
nandrolone.text: Nandrolone (Deca) is an injectable steroid used by lifters for muscle size and, per forum claims, bone growth and joint comfort. Trials show lean-mass gains in patients with illness, and none exist in healthy lifters.

chain: Easier to stay lean while dieting
oxandrolone.text: Oxandrolone (Anavar) is an oral steroid popular as a mild cutting compound, and some teens ask about it for height. Real trial data exist in burns and wasting, and the height claims conflict with growth studies.

stanozolol.text: Stanozolol (Winstrol) is a doping-famous steroid used for a dry, lean look, and forum posters also claim it masculinises the face or aids height. It is approved for hereditary angioedema, and appearance data are limited.

boldenone.text: Boldenone (Equipoise) is a veterinary steroid that bodybuilders use for slow, steady muscle gains. It is approved for horses rather than humans, and no human trials of its appearance effects exist.

chain: Rapid gain in lean mass and fullness
methandienone.text: Methandienone (Dianabol) is the classic oral bulking steroid in bodybuilding culture, used for fast mass gains, much of it water. Small controlled trials show lean-mass gains, while most claims rest on anecdote.

chain: Rapid mass, water and muscle fullness
oxymetholone.text: Oxymetholone (Anadrol) is an anemia drug that bodybuilders use as a powerful oral bulker for mass and fullness, and some forum posters say it masculinises the face and body. Its liver effects are well documented, while physique trials are almost absent.

drostanolone.text: Drostanolone (Masteron) is an injectable once used against breast cancer, now used by bodybuilders for a dry, hard, lean appearance. Forum posters also discuss its hair and skin effects. No trials examine appearance.

mesterolone.text: Mesterolone (Proviron) is a mild oral DHT derivative used medically for hypogonadism and fertility. Forum users add it for hardness, libido and puberty-maxxing and debate its effect on hair loss. Appearance effects are untested.

methyltestosterone.text: Methyltestosterone is an old oral testosterone analogue used medically for hypogonadism and in menopausal hormone therapy. Appearance and bodybuilding use is undocumented in trials and absent from the forum sources reviewed.

fluoxymesterone.text: Fluoxymesterone (Halotestin) is a strong oral androgen that bodybuilders add for hardness, strength and aggression more than size. Documented trials cover hypogonadism and breast cancer, and none examine appearance.

chain: Lean muscle gained with less water
methenolone.text: Methenolone (Primobolan) is a mild DHT-derived steroid prized in bodybuilding for lean gains with fewer side effects. Human trials exist in anemia, cancer and rehabilitation, and none address physique.
